row.title: Two-cycle list-coloring conjecture for planar graphs of girth at least five
row.statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least five, let $C_1,C_2$ be two cycles in $G$, and for every $v\in V(G)$ let $L(v)$ be a non-empty set such that $|L(v)|\ge 3$ for every $v\in V(G)-V(C_1)-V(C_2)$. A proper coloring from the lists is a map $\phi$ such that $\phi(v)\in L(v)$ for every vertex $v$. **Two-cycle list-coloring conjecture.** There exists a constant $K$ with the following property: if $G$ has no proper coloring $\phi$ from the lists, then $G$ has a subgraph $H$ on at most $K$ vertices such that $C_1$ and $C_2$ are subgraphs of $H$ and there exists no proper coloring $\psi$ of $H$ from the lists, meaning $\psi(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v\in V(H)$. This conjecture would extend the preceding result from ordinary 3-coloring to list-coloring for graphs of girth at least five, and the source presents that extension as an open problem.
row.source_name: Zdenek Dvorak, Daniel Kral and Robin Thomas, “Three-coloring triangle-free graphs on surfaces II. 4-critical graphs in a disk”, arXiv:1302.2158 (2017).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.2158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

row.title: Tatami covering generating-function coefficient conjecture
row.statement:
Let $V\!H_n(z)$ be the generating polynomial for maximal tatami coverings of the square grid with the relevant number of vertical or horizontal dominoes, and write $\langle z^k\rangle Q(z)$ for the coefficient of $z^k$ in a polynomial $Q(z)$. Let $\deg(V\!H_n(z))$ denote its degree. **Coefficient conjecture.**

(a) For $k\le n-2$,

$$
\langle z^{k}\rangle V\!H_n(z)=\langle z^{k}\rangle\prod_{m\ge 0}(1+z^m)^2,
$$

the number of partitions of $k$ into distinct parts with two types of each part.

(b) For $0\le k<n-3$,

$$
\langle z^{\deg(V\!H_n(z))-k}\rangle V\!H_n(z)=2\langle z^k\rangle\prod_{m\ge 0}(1+z^m),
$$

twice the number of partitions of $k$ into distinct parts.

These identities were verified computationally through at least $n=20$ and describe the low- and high-degree coefficients of the tatami-covering generating polynomial; a general proof is not supplied.
row.source_name: Alejandro Erickson and Frank Ruskey, “Enumerating maximal tatami mat coverings of square grids with v vertical dominoes”, arXiv:1304.0070 (2013).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.0070

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

row.title: The uniqueness conjecture for chord diagrams with genus range {1,2}
row.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let a **chord diagram** be represented by a double-occurrence word in which each letter occurs exactly twice; chord diagrams and words are considered up to the equivalence used in the paper. The genus range is the set of genera of the thickened chord diagrams associated with the chord diagram.

**Uniqueness conjecture for genus range $\{1,2\}$.** For any $n\neq 4$, there is a unique, up to equivalence, chord diagram with genus range

$$
\{1,2\},
$$

and it is represented by

$$
(123123)(44\cdots nn).
$$

The assertion is supported by the computed examples, while the paper gives no general proof. The excluded value $n=4$ is an exceptional case in the stated uniqueness claim.
row.source_name: Jonathan Burns, Nataša Jonoska and Masahico Saito, “Genus Ranges of Chord Diagrams”, arXiv:1410.6148 (2014).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.6148

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

row.title: The overhauled Roller-Coaster Conjecture for well-covered graphs of fixed order
row.statement:
Let $alpha\geq2$ and $n\geq4$ be integers satisfying

$$
2alpha\leq n\leq3alpha-2.
$$

For a graph $G$, let $alpha(G)$ denote its independence number, let $|V(G)|$ denote its order, and write $I(G;x)=\sum_k s_kx^k$ for its independence polynomial. **Overhauled Roller-Coaster Conjecture.** For every permutation $sigma$ of the set $\{\left\lceil \frac{alpha}{2}\right\rceil,ldots,\left\lceil \frac{n-1}{3}\right\rceil \}$, there exists a well-covered graph $G$ with $alpha(G)=alpha$ and $|V(G)|=n$ such that

$$
s_{sigma(\left\lceil \frac{alpha}{2}\right\rceil )}<s_{sigma(\left\lceil \frac{alpha}{2}\right\rceil +1)}<cdots<s_{sigma(\left\lceil \frac{n-1}{3}\right\rceil )}.
$$

This version records the proposed shortening of the index domain for well-covered graphs of order $n$; the source presents it as a conjectural overhauled formulation.
row.source_name: Vadim E. Levit and Eugen Mandrescu, “The Roller-Coaster Conjecture Revisited”, arXiv:1612.03736 (2016).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.03736

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

row.title: Existence conjecture for double blocking sets with two long secants
row.statement: Let $q$ be a prime power satisfying $q\geq 13$ and $q\not\equiv 2\pmod 3$. A **double blocking set** in $\operatorname{PG}(2,q)$ is a set meeting every line in at least two points; a **$(q-1)$-secant** is a line meeting it in exactly $q-1$ points. **Existence conjecture.** There exists a double blocking set in $\operatorname{PG}(2,q)$ of size $3q-1$ admitting two $(q-1)$-secants. The paper proposes this conjecture after refuting Hill's conjecture; the displayed constructions establish examples only for the listed values of $q$, so the general assertion remains open in the source.
row.source_name: Bence Csajbók and Tamás Héger, “Double blocking sets of size 3q-1 in PG(2,q)”, arXiv:1805.01267 (2019).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.01267

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

row.title: Large-order non-separating out-branching conjecture
row.statement: Let $D$ be a digraph on at least $K$ vertices. Write $\lambda(D)$ for its arc-connectivity and $\alpha(D)$ for its independence number. A **non-separating out-branching** is an out-branching whose deletion has the non-separation property studied in the paper. **Large-order non-separating out-branching conjecture.** There exists an integer $K$ such that every digraph $D$ on at least $K$ vertices with $\lambda(D)\geq 2$ and $\alpha(D)=2$ has a non-separating out-branching. The conjecture is motivated by a theorem establishing a bound of $14$ vertices; the source gives no resolution of the proposed existence of some universal $K$.
row.source_name: Joergen Bang-Jensen, Stéphane Bessy and Anders Yeo, “Non-separating spanning trees and out-branchings in digraphsof independence number 2”, arXiv:2007.02834 (2020).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.02834

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2020). “For instance it is an open problem whether the existence of vertex disjoint paths $P_1,P_2$ such that $P_i$ is an $(s_i,t_i)$-path for $i=1,2$ can be checked in polynomial time (for a partial result see ).”

row.title: The non-expanding links conjecture for bounded-degree graph sequences
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph. For a vertex subset $S\subset V_G$ with $0<\lvert S\rvert\leq \lvert G\rvert/2$, let $\partial S$ be its outer vertex boundary, and define the expansion of $G$ by

$$
h=\inf_{S\subset V_G:\,0<\lvert S\rvert\leq \lvert G\rvert/2}\frac{\lvert\partial S\rvert}{\lvert S\rvert}.
$$

The graph $G$ is an **$h$-expander** if its expansion is at least $h$, and a sequence of graphs is an **expander family** if some $h>0$ is a lower bound for the expansion of every graph in the sequence. The links are the graphs under consideration associated with the vertices and radii of the original graphs.

**Non-expanding links conjecture.** There is no sequence of bounded-degree finite graphs, with size growing to infinity, such that all links in all the graphs form an expander family.

This conjecture asserts that bounded degree and arbitrarily large graph size force at least some links to have vanishing expansion, despite the possibility that the original graphs may exhibit strong expansion. It concerns the interaction between local link structure and global graph expansion; the source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
row.source_name: Itai Benjamini and John Haslegrave, “Degrees in link graphs of regular graphs”, arXiv:2106.15464 (2022).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.15464

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

row.title: Higher-girth edge-girth-regular graph families
row.statement:
Let $q\geq 3$ be a prime power, and let $g\in\{8,12\}$. An $egr(v,k,g,\lambda)$-graph is an edge-girth-regular graph with order $v$, degree $k$, girth $g$, and each edge lying in exactly $\lambda$ cycles of length $g$.

**Higher-girth existence conjecture.** For $q\geq 3$ a prime power and $g\in\{8,12\}$, there exists a family of

$$
egr\left(2q^{\frac{g-2}{2}},q,g,(q-1)^{\frac{g-2}{2}}(q-2)\right)
$$

-graphs.

The conjecture is motivated by incidence graphs of generalized quadrangles and hexagons and by Moore-cage constructions. It predicts families with the indicated order and edge-girth parameters; no general construction or proof is supplied in the paper.
row.source_name: Araujo-Pardo Gabriela and Leemans Dimitri, “Edge-girth-regular graphs arising from biaffine planes and Suzuki groups”, arXiv:2108.06636 (2021).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.06636

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

row.title: Samsonov–Shur's conjecture on the Abelian repetition threshold
row.statement:
For a finite alphabet of size $k$, let ${\sf ART}(k)$ be the infimum of the real numbers $\alpha$ for which there exists an infinite $k$-ary Abelian $\alpha$-power-free word. The known lower bounds are

$$
{\sf ART}(4)\ge \frac{9}{5},\qquad {\sf ART}(k)\ge \frac{k-2}{k-3}\quad\text{for }k\ge 5.
$$

**Samsonov–Shur's conjecture.** The exact values are

$$
{\sf ART}(2)=\frac{11}{3};\qquad {\sf ART}(3)=2;\qquad {\sf ART}(4)=\frac{9}{5};\qquad {\sf ART}(k)=\frac{k-2}{k-3}\quad\text{for }k\ge 5.
$$

At the time of the paper, no exact values of ${\sf ART}(k)$ were known; the conjecture was proposed by Samsonov and Shur as a tightness assertion for their lower bounds. The present paper investigates these thresholds experimentally and shows that the proposed values are not correct in several cases.
row.source_name: Elena A. Petrova and Arseny M. Shur, “Abelian Repetition Threshold Revisited”, arXiv:2109.09306 (2021).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09306

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2021). “In , it was proved (Theorem 3.1) that $\ART(k)\ge \frac{k-2}{k-3}$ for all $k\ge 5$ and conjectured that the equality holds in all cases.”

row.title: Five-letter complete bifurcate-tree conjecture
row.statement:
A square-free word is **bifurcate** over an alphabet $\mathcal{A}$ if it has at least one square-free extension at every position. A complete bifurcate tree is an infinite rooted tree of bifurcate words in which every word of length $n$ has $n+1$ descendants, corresponding to extensions at the different positions, and every descendant remains bifurcate.

**Five-letter complete bifurcate-tree conjecture.** There exists a complete bifurcate tree over an alphabet of size $5$.

The paper proves that a complete bifurcate tree exists over alphabets of size at least $12$ and states that the five-letter bound is tight in the sense that a smaller alphabet cannot suffice. The supplied text does not report a resolution of the five-letter existence claim.
row.source_name: Michał Dębski, Jarosław Grytczuk and Bartłomiej Pawlik, “Extensions and reductions of square-free words”, arXiv:2209.08507 (2022).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.08507

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).

row.title: Corrected gucycle conjecture for unlabeled graphs
row.statement: Let a **gucycle** be a cyclic ordering whose windows represent each isomorphism class of graphs on $n$ vertices exactly once. **Corrected gucycle conjecture.** For each $n\geq 4$, there exists a gucycle of isomorphism classes of graphs on $n$ vertices. This corrects the Brockman–Kay–Snively conjecture, which fails for $n=3$; the general existence question remains unresolved in the source.
row.source_name: Rachel Kirsch, Clare Sibley and Elizabeth Sprangel, “Graph Universal Cycles: Compression and Connections to Universal Cycles”, arXiv:2209.14198 (2022).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.14198

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2022). “However, the following conjecture remains open.”

row.title: Lin's 3-adic congruence conjecture for the partition function $\text{PDO}_t(n)$
row.statement:
A partition with designated summands is obtained from an ordinary partition by tagging exactly one occurrence of each part size. Let $\text{PDO}_t(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ with designated summands in which every part is odd. For nonnegative integers $k$ and $n$, **Lin's conjecture.**

$$
\text{PDO}_t(8\cdot 3^k n)\equiv 0 \pmod{3^{k+2}},
$$

and

$$
\text{PDO}_t(12\cdot 3^k n)\equiv 0 \pmod{3^{k+2}}.
$$

These congruences extend Lin's known congruences modulo $9$ and $27$. The conjecture is open for general $k$; the source paper proves the cases needed for $k=0,1,2$.
row.source_name: Gurinder Singh and Rupam Barman, “Congruences for the partition function PDO_t(n) modulo powers of 2 and 3”, arXiv:2307.04687 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04687

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2023). “The conjecture is open for general $k$.”

row.title: The non-3-colorability conjecture for countable undirected multigraphs
row.statement:
An **undirected countable multigraph** is a countable undirected graph whose edges have weights in $\mathbb{N}$. A majority coloring is a coloring such that, at every vertex, the total weight of bichromatic incident edges is at least the total weight of monochromatic incident edges.

**Multigraph non-3-colorability conjecture.** There exists an undirected countable multigraph that is not majority 3-colorable.

Finite multigraphs are majority 2-colorable by a max-cut argument, but the directed construction in the paper does not directly transfer to multigraphs. The asserted countable example remains open in the source.
row.source_name: Bartłomiej Bosek and Aleksander Katan, “A Note About Majority Colorings of Countable DAGs”, arXiv:2406.04189 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04189

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

row.title: The path-linked triangles 3-colourability conjecture
row.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph which is a disjoint union of triangles and paths of length at most $12$, and let $G$ be obtained from $H$ by gluing on vertex-disjoint triangles. For two triangles $T,T'$ in $H$, say they are **path-linked** if there exists a glued-in triangle $Y$ with $T\cap Y,T'\cap Y\neq\emptyset$ and the third vertex of $Y$ lies on a path in $G$ of length at least two. **Path-linked triangles conjecture.** If every $H$-triangle in $G$ is path-linked to at most one other $H$-triangle, then $G$ is 3-colourable.

The restrictions are intended to avoid the known obstructions arising from more general unions of paths and triangles; the case where all $H$-paths have length at most $2$ follows from an auxiliary bipartite-graph argument. The conjecture is presented as approachable, but remains open in the source.
row.source_name: Aseem Dalal, Jessica McDonald and Songling Shan, “A reduction of the "cycles plus K_4's" problem”, arXiv:2406.17723 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17723

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2024). “On the other hand, while the truth of the Strong Colouring Conjecture is trivial for $\Delta(H)=1$, (where it asks essentially for the union of two matchings to be bipartite), the $\Delta(H)=c$ case is open for all constants $c\geq 2$.”

row.title: Sheehan's uniquely Hamiltonian regular graph conjecture
row.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple $k$-regular graph, where a graph is **uniquely Hamiltonian** if it has exactly one Hamiltonian circuit. **Sheehan's conjecture.** There are no uniquely Hamiltonian $k$-regular graphs for any integer $k\geq 3$. This extends the parity obstruction for odd-regular multigraphs and remains open for general regular graphs of degree at least three.
row.source_name: D. Labbate and F. Romaniello, “An updated survey on 2-Factors of Regular Graphs”, arXiv:2408.04642 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04642

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

row.title: Expander-family conjecture for undirected prefix-reversal graphs
row.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}_m(n)$ be the undirected prefix-reversal graph, which is $2n$-regular for $m>1$. A sequence of regular graphs is an **expander family** if there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that every graph in the sequence has expansion ratio at least $\varepsilon$. **Expander-family conjecture.** Given $n\geq1$, the sequence of $2n$-regular graphs

$$
\{\mathbb{P}_m(n)\}_{m>1}
$$

indexed by $m$ is an expander family of graphs. The conjecture concerns expansion as $m$ varies with $n$ fixed; the source provides no resolution.
row.source_name: Saúl A. Blanco and Charles Buehrle, “On the spectra of prefix-reversal graphs”, arXiv:2506.08345 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08345

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

row.title: Localization capture time conjecture for connected graphs
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $\operatorname{lcapt}(G)$ denote its localization capture time, namely the minimum number of rounds needed for the minimum number $\zeta(G)$ of cops to locate an omniscient robber on $G$. A family of graphs is **well-localizable** if there exists a constant $D$ such that every graph $G$ in the family satisfies

$$
\operatorname{lcapt}(G)\leq D|V(G)|.
$$

**Localization Capture Time Conjecture (LCTC).** The family of all connected graphs is well-localizable; equivalently, there exists a constant $D$ such that every connected graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{lcapt}(G)\leq D|V(G)|.
$$

This conjecture seeks a linear upper bound on localization capture time in terms of the number of vertices. Exact bounds are known for several graph families, including trees and outerplanar graphs, but the general connected-graph case remains open.
row.source_name: Vesna Iršič Chenoweth and Matija Skrt, “Localization game capture time of trees and outerplanar graphs”, arXiv:2508.10443 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10443

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

row.title: Bounded cliquewidth under proper separator decompositions
row.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal B$ be classes of graphs closed under taking induced subgraphs. Suppose that every 2-connected graph in $\mathcal C$ is either in $\mathcal B$ or has a proper 2-separator or a proper $P_3$-separator. Assume that, for some constant $a$, every graph in $\mathcal B$ has cliquewidth at most $a$.

**Cliquewidth preservation conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that every graph in $\mathcal C$ has cliquewidth at most $f(a)$.

This conjecture asks whether decomposing graphs along proper 2-separators and proper $P_3$-separators preserves bounded cliquewidth. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
row.source_name: Beatriz Martins and Nicolas Trotignon, “(Even hole, triangle)-free graphs revisited”, arXiv:2604.01816 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01816

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

row.title: Permutation conjecture for prime-exponent LCMs of distinct covering systems
row.statement:
A **distinct covering system** is a covering system whose moduli are distinct integers greater than $1$. Let $m\geq 2$, let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be positive integers, and let $L$ denote the least common multiple of its moduli. For a permutation $(a_1,b_1,c_1)$ of $(a,b,c)$ with $a_1\geq b_1\geq c_1$, **the permutation conjecture.** If there exists a distinct covering system with least modulus $m$ and

$$
L=2^a3^b5^c,
$$

then there exists a distinct covering system with least modulus $m$ and

$$
L=2^{a_1}3^{b_1}5^{c_1}.
$$

The conjecture motivates restricting the analysis to exponents ordered as $a\geq b\geq c$. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
row.source_name: Joshua Harrington, Jonah Klein, Joshua Lowrance and Ognian Trifonov, “Covering systems where the prime divisors of all moduli are only 2, 3, or 5”, arXiv:2605.18644 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18644

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

row.title: Linear connected matching conjecture for graphs with independence number two
row.statement: There is a constant \(c>0\) such that every graph \(G\) on \(n\ge 3\) vertices with \(\alpha(G)=2\) contains a connected matching of size \(cn\).
row.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2025/1, page 21
